routes.note: Only camp listed, and it is the standard off-trail high camp directly under the peak; confidence is high.

main: White Chuck Glacier basin, under Kololo Peaks
Sloan Creek Campground and the North Fork Sauk road end
routes.note: White Chuck Glacier basin is the climbing camp used to attempt the peak; Sloan Creek/North Fork Sauk road end is the standard staging camp the night before; Mackinaw Shelter, about five miles in, is a common first-night stop for parties splitting the approach into three days.

main: Mount Pugh road end, Forest Road 2095
Lake Metan, Mount Pugh trail
onRoute: Stujack Pass and the benches just below it
routes.note: Most parties climb Pugh car-to-car from the road end; Lake Metan is the one established camp used when the day is split; Stujack Pass is a higher bivy on the route itself for an alpine-start push, not a typical overnight base.

main: Sloan Creek Campground and the North Fork Sauk road end
routes.note: Painted Mountain is done as a day trip from the North Fork Sauk road end; no higher camp is used or listed.

main: One Acre Lake, under Mount Stickney

drop: San Juan Campground, Index-Galena road
routes.note: San Juan Campground sits on Index-Galena Road, a different corridor from the Sultan Basin Road approach this route actually uses, so it was dropped; One Acre Lake is the one worthwhile camp on the peak itself.

main: San Juan Campground, Index-Galena road
onRoute: Spire Mountain — the saddle northwest of the summit
routes.note: Spire Mountain has no established camp; most parties climb it car-to-car from the North Fork Skykomish trailhead off Index-Galena Road, staging the night before at San Juan Campground, with the summit-saddle bivy as a fallback for a slow party.

main: Gunn Basin, below Tailgunner Pass
Barclay Creek roadhead pullouts
San Juan Campground, Index-Galena road
routes.note: Gunn Basin is the high camp that turns a long day comfortable; the roadhead pullouts and San Juan Campground are both staging options the night before, progressively farther from the climbers' path.

routes.note: Every listed camp belongs to the Burgundy Col approach on the opposite side of the mountain; this route starts at the separate Cedar Creek Trailhead near Mazama, so all six were dropped and the nearest real campground was added. The route is often done car-to-car in one long day, and no established on-route camp is confirmed.
